rejected.title: Building the pyramids
card: The great pyramids at Giza were built as tombs for pharaohs. They were built about 4,500 years ago, and the biggest is the Great Pyramid of Khufu.

Many people once believed that slaves built the pyramids. That idea came from some later writers, who lived long after the pyramids were built. A source from long after an event may be less reliable than evidence from the time.
Archaeologists have dug up villages near Giza where the workers lived. They found bakeries, sleeping areas and large amounts of bread, beef and fish bones.
This evidence suggests that teams of fed and housed workers built the pyramids, not slaves. New archaeological finds changed what historians believed.
rejected.remember: Evidence from the workers' villages changed an old view: the pyramids seem to have been built by teams of fed and housed workers.

a.q: Which find best supports the view that the pyramid builders were fed and housed?
opts: Bakeries and food remains in a village near Giza
A pharaoh's name carved inside a pyramid tomb
A story about slaves written long after the pyramids
Gold goods buried with a pharaoh in his tomb
a.why: Bakeries and food remains show that the workers lived nearby and were given meals. A story written long after the pyramids does not come from the time and cannot show how workers were treated.
a.clue: Look for evidence from where the workers lived.

b.q: A tour guide tells Amir that slaves built the pyramids. The guide quotes a Greek writer who visited Egypt about 2,000 years after they were built. Why do historians now doubt this claim?
opts: Remains of workers' villages point to fed and housed teams
The Greek writer lived too early to know much about Egypt
Visitors to a place are always unreliable as sources
No one has ever found where the pyramid workers lived
b.why: Digs at villages near Giza found bakeries, sleeping areas and food remains, which suggest fed and housed teams did the work. The writer lived long after the pyramids, not too early. A later source may be less reliable, but that does not make every visitor always unreliable.
b.clue: What did archaeologists find near Giza?
